paths.description: Homepage/listing archetype and primary article-discovery journey; tested desktop, 360px mobile, dark/reduced-motion preferences, keyboard focus, accessibility, performance, network, security, privacy, and memory.
Current article/detail archetype representing the core reading journey; tested desktop, mobile layout, crawler visibility, and image delivery.
Terms/policy archetype used to verify legal-content rendering and language consistency.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-color preference
findings.evidence: A dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light rendering and the computed root colorScheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Text contrast is insufficient across article metadata
findings.evidence: axe reports 78 serious color-contrast failures on homepage article authors and dates.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/background contrast to WCAG AA and verify under high-contrast preferences.

findings.summary: Navigation changes have no continuity cue
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no active animations or authored transition use on a link-heavy publication experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Use restrained cross-document view transitions for article navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-progress or state-aware navigation
findings.evidence: The article content is 10,650px tall, while screenshots and DOM show no progress indicator or state-aware reading chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading-progress indicator or compact sticky article context.

findings.summary: Consent UI blocks the entire reading experience on arrival
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-page dimmer and consent prompt before any article can be read.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the initial consent choice compact, responsive, and non-obscuring while preserving a clear decline option.

findings.summary: Consent dialogs are not robust semantic modals and fail on mobile
findings.evidence: Four role=dialog nodes lack aria-modal; at 360px the panel is mostly off-screen and produces 778px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog/top-layer pattern with aria-modal, focus containment, Escape handling, and responsive inline sizing.

findings.summary: Advertising and tracking machinery dominates page cost and attention
findings.evidence: HAR records 145 requests, 140 third-party requests, 63 scripts, and 68 third-party origins while the consent overlay obscures content.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising and recommendation chrome until needed and after a valid choice.

findings.summary: The mobile experience overflows by 778px
findings.evidence: Layout at a 360px viewport reports scrollWidth 1138px, clientWidth 360px, and horizontalOverflowPx 778 on both home and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop widths and constrain every overlay and content component to the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Core components do not adapt to the available inline size
findings.evidence: The consent panel is clipped almost completely at 360px and the layout retains a 1138px CSS width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container/media queries, minmax(), and max-inline-size:100% for cards, article columns, and overlays.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is visually suppressed
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none for all 30 sampled visible interactive elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator without removing native outlines.

findings.summary: The primary reading journey is blocked by a broken mobile consent step
findings.evidence: At 360px only the right edge of the consent surface is visible, leaving its choice buttons off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Make both consent choices reachable at all supported viewports and test the full decline/continue journey.

findings.summary: Loading performance is far outside good thresholds
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse reports performance 0.37, FCP 6.3s, LCP 18.1s, TBT 770ms, and Speed Index 18.4s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce server latency, and delay ad/analytics work until after useful content.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript keeps the main thread busy
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 6.9s main-thread work, 4.4s JavaScript execution, and 770ms TBT; the HAR contains 63 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer low-value tags, split long tasks, and schedule non-urgent work after interaction readiness.

findings.summary: The page transfers a large, mostly third-party payload
findings.evidence: HAR records 3.08MB in one capture; Lighthouse records 4,886KiB and 1,482KiB potential cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit resource priorities and caching, compress assets, and defer non-critical third parties.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped CSS and JavaScript are unused
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,311KiB unused JavaScript and 62KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory bundles and tags, remove duplicate/unused code, and load route-specific code on demand.

findings.summary: Interactive controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: axe finds an unnamed search button and five unnamed pagination/social links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only control a visible or programmatic accessible name.

findings.summary: Secondary text fails minimum contrast
findings.evidence: axe reports 78 serious contrast failures, concentrated in bylines and publication dates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AA-compliant semantic color tokens and test all states.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark, and focus structure is unreliable
findings.evidence: axe reports incorrect heading order and a nested complementary landmark; the probe also shows no visible outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair heading hierarchy and landmark placement, then implement visible focus and modal focus management.

findings.summary: Zoom and mobile reflow are restricted or broken
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags a restrictive viewport and undersized touch targets; raw mobile layout overflows 778px.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit user zoom, reflow to 320 CSS px, and size touch targets to at least 44px with spacing.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the console-errors audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve runtime and network errors and monitor regressions in production.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery metadata are incomplete
findings.evidence: The article image audit finds 16 images without dimensions, 10 without srcset, and eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources, and native lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser issues remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated API warning and DevTools Issues failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs and clear browser issue-panel warnings.

findings.summary: Crawler-visible content is sparse and mobile rendering is broken
findings.evidence: Raw-HTML coverage is 32% on home and 29% on article; mobile layout overflows 778px.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render primary listing/article text and fix responsive layout without hiding content behind client work.

findings.summary: No structured data describes the publication content
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds zero application/ld+json blocks on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add valid Organization/WebSite and Article JSON-LD with canonical, image, author, and dates.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie transport controls are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP and HSTS are missing; 16 of 20 observed cookies lack Secure, including the Rails session cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and a nonce/hash CSP, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with appropriate SameSite and HttpOnly.

findings.summary: Tracking starts with an extreme third-party footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker capture sees 68 third-party origins and 13 known tracker domains; HAR attributes 140 of 145 requests and 3.04MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to data minimisation: block non-essential tags before consent and remove vendors without clear user value.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: CSP and Permissions-Policy are absent, although nosniff, SAMEORIGIN, and strict-origin referrer policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP and least-privilege Permissions-Policy, retaining existing defensive headers.

findings.summary: Runtime errors reduce resilience
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports console errors and deprecated API use on the primary path.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle third-party failures defensively and remove deprecated/runtime-erroring code.

findings.summary: Non-essential tracking occurs while consent is still being requested
findings.evidence: The initial screenshot shows the consent request, while the same fresh-load tracker capture already records 68 third-party origins and known ad/analytics trackers.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize non-essential vendors until an affirmative choice; make reject and accept equally clear.

findings.summary: Assets are not delivered efficiently
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a 4,886KiB page and 288KiB image-delivery savings; article images lack dimensions and srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Resize and responsively encode images, set dimensions, and remove unused payload.

findings.summary: Unused code and tag execution waste CPU and energy
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,311KiB unused JS, 6.9s main-thread work, and 4.4s JS execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate unused code and batch/deprioritize non-visible analytics and ad work.

findings.summary: There is no effective third-party performance budget
findings.evidence: HAR shows 140 third-party requests and 3.04MB third-party transfer on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable request/byte/CPU budgets and load vendors only after consent and idle.

findings.summary: Public content lacks machine-readable structure and has low no-JS coverage
findings.evidence: The public article has only 29% raw/rendered content-word coverage and homepage has no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose robust server-rendered semantics and JSON-LD; consider explicit agent tools only for real user tasks.

findings.summary: The initial page has a very large DOM/heap footprint
findings.evidence: Baseline heap contains 896,651 nodes, 3,832,781 edges, and 47.6MB self size before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce embedded vendor DOM/iframes and defer offscreen widgets and recommendation trees.
